requirements.title: TimelineItem is the single persisted unit of a conversation, with id, optional turnID, date and a tagged content union
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:3-14 struct TimelineItem - Codable, Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable; fields id: String, turnID: UUID?, date: Date, content: Content; init defaults id = UUID().uuidString and date = .now
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:16-25 enum Content - the eight cases the timeline can hold
requirements.preconditions: A thread document is being built in memory or decoded from disk.
requirements.action: The runtime appends or decodes a timeline item.
requirements.expected_result: Every item carries exactly four stored fields: id (String, defaulting to a fresh UUID string), turnID (UUID or null), date (Date, defaulting to now) and content, which is exactly one of user, assistant, reasoning, tool, plan, todos, notice, turnEnd. No other case exists and no other field is stored.
requirements.persistence: Serialized inside ThreadDocument.items under the JSON keys id, turnID, date, content; the content union is encoded by Swift's synthesized enum coding, i.e. a single-key object whose key is the case name.
failure_cases: An item that fails to decode is dropped rather than failing the whole document (see PR-CHAT-019).
requirements.windows_path: A discriminated-union record type in the Windows model layer, serialized with the same key names and the same single-key-object shape for the union, so a thread written by either build round-trips.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture: encode/decode round-trip against a pinned JSON fixture per content case

requirements.title: A reasoning block whose text is only whitespace is flagged empty
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:27-31 TimelineItem.isEmptyReasoning - guard case .reasoning(let block); returns block.text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
requirements.preconditions: A timeline item exists.
requirements.action: Anything asks the item whether it is empty reasoning.
requirements.expected_result: True only when the content is .reasoning and its text trims to the empty string over the Unicode whitespace-and-newlines set. Every other content case returns false, including an assistant message with empty text.
requirements.windows_path: Trim against the same Unicode whitespace and newline set (not ASCII-only), because a redacted reasoning stream can leave non-breaking or line-separator characters behind.
requirements.verification_method: unit

requirements.title: Em-dash cleanup rewrites only model-written prose, never the user's words, tool output or notices
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:34-55 TimelineItem.cleanedOfEmDashes - switches on .assistant, .reasoning and .plan only; default: break leaves user, tool, todos, notice and turnEnd untouched
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:42 message.text = TextCleanup.withoutEmDashes(message.text)
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:48 plan.markdown = TextCleanup.withoutEmDashes(plan.markdown)
requirements.preconditions: A stored thread is read back that was written by a build which cleaned text only as it arrived.
requirements.action: The item is passed through cleanedOfEmDashes.
requirements.expected_result: assistant.text, reasoning.text and plan.markdown are replaced by TextCleanup.withoutEmDashes of themselves. user, tool, todos, notice and turnEnd items are returned byte-identical. The item's id, turnID and date are preserved.
requirements.persistence: Applied to items as read; the cleaned value is what subsequent writes persist.
requirements.windows_path: Same three cases only. Do not extend the cleanup to tool output: a command's stdout containing an em dash must survive verbatim.
requirements.verification_method: unit: one fixture item per content case, asserting only the three named cases change

requirements.title: UserMessage carries text, attachments and two optional Hydra markers that decide which row draws it
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:57-69 struct UserMessage - text: String, attachments: [Attachment] = [], hydraHeads: [Int]?, hydraBrief: Bool?; isFromHydra is hydraHeads != nil; isHydraBrief is hydraBrief == true
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/TimelineRows.swift:79-83 UserMessageRow - isFromHydra routes to HydraReportRow, isHydraBrief routes to HydraBriefRow, otherwise the plain bubble
requirements.preconditions: A user-kind timeline item is about to be rendered.
requirements.expected_result: hydraHeads present (even as an empty array) means the message is Hydra's, not the user's, and it draws as HydraReportRow. hydraHeads absent and hydraBrief == true draws as HydraBriefRow. Neither draws the plain user bubble. hydraBrief being absent or false is not a brief. The isFromHydra test precedes the isHydraBrief test.
requirements.persistence: hydraHeads and hydraBrief are optional JSON keys, absent on messages stored before they existed, and their absence decodes as nil without failing.
requirements.windows_path: Keep the three-way branch and its order. Windows must distinguish an absent hydraHeads key from an empty array: an empty array is a note from Hydra itself and still takes the report row.
requirements.verification_method: unit plus interaction test over the three branches

requirements.title: Attachment identifies a file by path and mime type, and is an image when the mime type starts with image/
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:88-96 struct Attachment - id = UUID(), name, path, mimeType; url is URL(fileURLWithPath: path); isImage is mimeType.hasPrefix("image/")
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:99-105 Attachment.base64Images - @concurrent, compactMap over attachments, keeps only isImage entries whose bytes read, returns (image, base64)
requirements.preconditions: A message carries attachments.
requirements.action: The UI or the provider path asks whether an attachment is an image, or asks for the base64 images.
requirements.expected_result: isImage is a literal prefix test on the mimeType string against "image/", never on the file extension. base64Images reads each image's bytes off the main actor and silently skips any attachment whose bytes cannot be read, returning only the pairs that succeeded, in the original order.
side_effects: base64Images reads each image file from disk
requirements.persistence: id, name, path and mimeType are persisted with the message.
failure_cases: A file that cannot be read is dropped from the result with no error and no notice.
requirements.windows_path: URL(fileURLWithPath:) becomes a Windows absolute path; the stored path is the platform path as captured. Base64 encoding must run off the UI thread: the source comment records that a photo is megabytes and its string a third larger again.
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fixture directory including one unreadable path

requirements.title: ToolCall has exactly eight kinds and four statuses, and both are persisted as their lowercase raw strings

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:130-135 enum ToolCall.Status: String - running, completed, failed, declined

requirements.preconditions: A provider event creates or updates a tool call.
requirements.action: The call is written into the timeline.
requirements.expected_result: kind is one of the eight literals command, read, edit, search, web, mcp, agent, other. status is one of running, completed, failed, declined and defaults to running. output defaults to the empty string, edits to an empty array, startedAt to now, and detail, exitCode and finishedAt are null until set.

requirements.title: Tool output is trimmed to a 60000-byte ceiling by replacing the head with a single ellipsis and keeping the last 30000 bytes
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:137 static let outputLimit = 60_000
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:149-157 appendOutput appends then trims; setOutput replaces then trims
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:164-167 trimOutput - guard output.utf8.count > Self.outputLimit; output = "…" + String(output.suffix(Self.outputLimit / 2))
requirements.preconditions: A tool call is streaming or has just received its whole output.
requirements.expected_result: While the output's UTF-8 byte count is at most 60000 it is kept whole. Above that the output becomes the single character U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS followed by the last 30000 Characters of the current output. Note that the guard counts UTF-8 bytes while suffix counts Characters, so the trimmed result can still exceed 60000 bytes for non-ASCII output; this is the shipped behavior.
requirements.persistence: The trimmed value is what is stored in the item and written to disk.
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the byte-count guard and the Character-count suffix exactly, including the unit mismatch. Windows string indices are UTF-16 code units: suffix must be taken over grapheme clusters, not code units, or a surrogate pair is split.
requirements.verification_method: unit with an ASCII case, a CJK case and an emoji case at the boundary

requirements.title: finish() sets the status and stamps finishedAt only the first time
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:159-162 finish(_ status:) - self.status = status; if finishedAt == nil { finishedAt = .now }
requirements.preconditions: A tool call exists.
requirements.action: finish is called, possibly more than once.
requirements.expected_result: status is overwritten every time. finishedAt is written only when it is currently null, so a second finish never moves the recorded end time. The elapsed duration a row shows therefore never grows after the first completion.
requirements.persistence: status and finishedAt on the tool item.
requirements.windows_path: Same first-write-wins rule on finishedAt.
requirements.verification_method: unit

requirements.title: TurnRecord decodes field by field with per-field defaults so a turn written by an older build is never dropped
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:249-273 struct TurnRecord - id, index, providerTurnID, startedAt, completedAt, status, baseCheckpoint, endCheckpoint, userItemID, providerDiff, providerAnchor, touchedPaths, tokenSpends, hydraMerged = false

requirements.title: Array members of a thread document decode leniently: an unreadable item is dropped, never the document
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Timeline.swift:322-331 ThreadDocument.init(from:) - items, turns, followUps and hydraMerges each decode as [Lenient<T>] with an empty-array default, then .compactMap(\.value)

requirements.title: The timeline's shared geometry is eight named constants and everything in the column derives from them

requirements.title: While the window is being reshaped the rows wrap to a width quantized to 12 points and capped at 860
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:59 private static let resizeStep: CGFloat = 12

DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:60-68 layoutWidth - nil unless liveResize.isReshaping and paneWidth > 0; sidebar sliding returns min(820 + 40, max(resizeStep, paneWidthAtSlideStart + model.sidebar.slideDelta)); otherwise min(820 + 40, (paneWidth / 12).rounded(.down) * 12)
requirements.preconditions: The window is being dragged, the sidebar is sliding or dragging, or the terminal divider is held.
requirements.expected_result: The content lays out at a stepped width so rows re-measure a few times over a drag rather than every frame. During the sidebar's slide the rows wrap once at the pane's final width (start width plus the slide delta) and the pane clips them as it moves. Both are capped at 860 (820 + 40) and floored at 12. When nothing is reshaping, layoutWidth is null and the natural width applies exactly.

requirements.title: The measured viewport height is quantized to 12 points and written only when it moves
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:425-428 onGeometryChange of visibleHeight - let stepped = (height / resizeStep).rounded(.down) * resizeStep; if stepped != viewportHeight { viewportHeight = stepped }

requirements.title: Entries are partitioned into contiguous runs sharing one turn id, and each run with a turn id becomes exactly one block

requirements.title: A viewport that has ended up past the end of the content snaps back to the end on the next main-queue turn

requirements.verification_method: interaction test: wheel-scroll up during a streaming turn and assert the view stays put

requirements.title: Accumulated drift past a tolerance tells the lazy list where the viewport is
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:496-520 the at-rest branch - shrink = max(0, old.contentHeight - new.contentHeight); drift is the anchor-compensated offset move; noteDrift(shrink + drift, tolerance:) arms a viewport refresh when the running total exceeds the tolerance; a shrink over one point also arms the blank watch; the reader's own scrolling resets the drift
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:807-809 jumpTolerance - max(48, viewportHeight / 4)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:1120-1131 noteDrift adds and returns true once past the tolerance, zeroing the total; resetDrift zeroes it
requirements.preconditions: The content changes shape under a resting reader.
requirements.expected_result: Growth the bottom anchor follows is not counted as drift, since the row that grew is the row under the viewport. Everything else accumulates, because a fold under an animation moves the viewport a little each frame. Once the total passes the greater of 48 points and a quarter of the viewport height, the lazy list is told where the viewport is and the total starts again.
requirements.windows_path: Only needed where the list virtualizes against a remembered viewport. If the Windows list recomputes visible range from the live scroll offset every frame, this becomes a no-op; say so explicitly rather than porting a dead mechanism.
requirements.verification_method: unit over the drift accumulator plus an interaction test folding a turn under an animation

requirements.title: A timeline showing nothing repairs itself in three escalating steps and then stops
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:744-777 repairLayout - requires viewportHeight > 0; defers while the reader scrolls, coasts or the rows are frozen, setting repairSkippedWhileScrolling; past the end or pinned-and-away it snaps to the end first; when showing nothing it runs case 0 refreshViewport, case 1 stackGeneration += 1 then arm a refresh, case 2 pin to the bottom, snap and arm a refresh, default return; then blankRepairs += 1 and the blank watch is re-armed
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:976-990 setVisible - a row appearing cancels the blank watch and zeroes blankRepairs; the last row leaving arms the watch
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:952-955 showsNothing - there are rows to show and none of them is on screen
requirements.preconditions: A layout pass has left the viewport over space the lazy list built nothing for.
requirements.action: The blank watch fires, a stalled scroll phase is cleared, or the reader returns to the front.
requirements.expected_result: First the list is told where the viewport is. Still blank a beat later, the list is rebuilt from scratch and told again. Still blank, the timeline pins to the end, snaps there and tells the list again. A fourth blank in a row is left alone. Any row coming back on screen ends the sequence and resets the counter.
failure_cases: A repair requested while the reader is scrolling is remembered and run when the scroll ends (ThreadTimeline.swift:455-464).
requirements.windows_path: Only required where the list virtualizes. The escalation order and the three-attempt cap are part of the contract; an unbounded retry loop is not acceptable.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test forcing a blank viewport

requirements.title: The blank watch looks 300 milliseconds later and asks for a check only if still blank
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:1099-1106 armBlankWatch - cancels the previous watch, sleeps 300 ms, and bumps checkRequest only when not cancelled and showsNothing
requirements.preconditions: Rows exist and none is on screen, or something changed shape.
requirements.expected_result: Exactly one pending watch at a time; re-arming cancels the previous one. After 300 milliseconds, if rows are still showing nothing, a layout check is requested.
requirements.cancellation: Cancelled by a row reporting itself visible, by re-arming, or by the view going away.
requirements.windows_path: A single cancellable timer per timeline.
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fake clock

requirements.title: A scroll phase whose end is never delivered is cleared by a watchdog with per-phase and absolute ceilings
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:1067-1094 notePhase - isUserScrolling for interacting or decelerating, isCoasting for decelerating or animating; an interacting phase resets the drift; the watch polls every 200 ms and ends the phase when the reader has not moved the offset for `still` seconds (2.0 for interacting, 0.4 otherwise) or the phase has run 3.0 seconds; ending the phase withdraws the scroll-activity report and bumps checkRequest
requirements.preconditions: A scroll phase is reported.
requirements.action: The phase's end event is lost, for instance because content grew under an animated scroll or the app went to the back mid-flick.
requirements.expected_result: The phase is force-ended after the stillness window or the three-second ceiling, whichever comes first, and a layout check is requested. Without it the timeline would count itself as moving for good and never snap or repair again, which the source records as leaving a running turn the reader could not see until the thread was reopened.
side_effects: ScrollActivity.shared is told this timeline has stopped scrolling, which lets shimmers and animations elsewhere resume
requirements.cancellation: A new phase report cancels the watch.
requirements.windows_path: Windows scroll events differ, but the watchdog is mandatory: any scroll-phase state the port keeps must have an equivalent timeout, with the same 2.0 / 0.4 / 3.0 seconds.
requirements.verification_method: unit with a fake clock plus an interaction test that drops the end event

requirements.title: Rows stop answering hover and hit tests while the content moves under the pointer, lifting 150 milliseconds after the last moved frame
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:701-719 noteScrollMovement - records the movement time; on the first movement sets isReaderScrolling, reports the activity, cancels the settle watch and starts one that polls every 80 ms and clears the flag once 0.15 seconds have passed with no movement
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:721-726 liftScrollFreeze - cancels the watch and clears the flag at once
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:2292-2297 ScrollFreeze - content.allowsHitTesting(!tracking.isReaderScrolling)
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/ThreadTimeline.swift:442-452 onScrollPhaseChange - .interacting notes movement, every other phase lifts the freeze
requirements.preconditions: The reader drags, flicks or wheels the timeline.
requirements.action: Frames move under a resting pointer.
requirements.expected_result: The rows stop hit-testing, so SwiftUI does not re-hit-test every row's hover region each frame and flip hover states as rows pass. The freeze lifts 150 milliseconds after the last moved frame, or immediately when a scroll phase other than interacting is reported, so a click that stops a flick always reaches its target. The flag lives on the tracking object and is read only by this leaf modifier, so its flips never re-render the timeline body.
requirements.cancellation: The watch is cancelled when the view disappears (endActivity).
requirements.windows_path: Windows equivalent is disabling pointer events on the list during scroll. The source measures this as a fifth of the main thread's scroll-time work, so it is a performance requirement, not cosmetic.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: hover a row, wheel-scroll, assert no hover state change until 150 ms after the last tick
